title: Port OS concepts
description: Use this guide to learn the Port OS vocabulary: endpoints, capabilities, groups and permissions.
content:
# Port OS concepts

A principal is an account identity governed by authorization rules. An endpoint is the stable device abstraction you query and address by full ID. Plugin routes provide ways to reach device functionality; multiple routes can contribute to one endpoint. A capability declares supported messages and observations with a namespace and version. A message combines that capability header with a schema-valid body.

Endpoints belong to groups; groups may be nested. Group/room names help selection but are not unique identity. Use full IDs and context. Deduplicate nested membership. Sharing expands only the resources/actions explicitly granted to the current principal.

The normal flow is discovery → capability schema → authorized message → observation. The [API guide](/docs/for-ai/guides/using-the-api.md) explains transport, and [the capability directory](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces.md) supplies contracts. Public guides describe supported devices; retired hosted task/filesystem features are outside this setup.

title: Verify the connection and control one light
description: Use this guide to confirm that a new connection works by reading and controlling one light.
content:
# Verify the connection and control one light

First complete [OAuth setup](/docs/for-ai/guides/authentication-and-dcr.md). Keep the discovered API issuer and credentials in client configuration.

1. GET /endpoints?owner=~caller&maxResults=25 with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Collection requests default to enabled endpoints owned by the caller; `owner=~caller` makes that scope explicit. POST /endpoint-query with `{}` has the same owner-scoped default. Type and capability filters stay within the caller's endpoints; an explicit owner, endpoint ID, or authorized group selector can include readable shared endpoints. Read [enumerateEndpoints](/docs/for-ai/operations/enumerateEndpoints.md) and [endpointQuery](/docs/for-ai/operations/endpointQuery.md) for pagination and request fields. Follow continuation metadata until enumeration is complete. An empty list means valid access with no visible devices; guide the user to [add devices](/docs/for-ai/guides/adding-devices.md).
2. Select one light by full endpoint ID and group/room context. If the target is ambiguous, ask the user before acting.
3. Inspect its declared capability namespace and version. A light declaring power 1.0 uses the [power guide](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces/power/1.0.md) and [turn-on payload schema](/docs/references/capability-interfaces/power/1.0/messages/turn-on.yaml). For other versions or capabilities, follow [the capability directory](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces.md).
4. With the user's intended action, POST /messages with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and Content-Type: application/json. Send the request object below as the JSON body, without a surrounding `body` field or a JSON string. Read [sendMessage](/docs/for-ai/operations/sendMessage.md) and its linked request schema. Use the endpoint ID and message version you discovered, not the illustrative ID below.

```json
{"target":{"type":"ENDPOINT","id":"port1/principals/example/endpoints/example-light"},"message":{"header":{"namespace":"port1/systems/zero/capability-interfaces/power","name":"turn-on","version":"1.0"},"body":{}}}
```

HTTP 200 acknowledges acceptance. An asynchronous request can return `{"messageId":""}` without a `message`; the empty ID is valid and does not provide a durable receipt or retry deduplication. When a unary response message is present, `messageId` identifies that response. Neither response proves physical state. After a lost response, treat the outcome as unknown and inspect state before deciding whether another action is safe.

Do not cut JSON with head -c. GET /endpoints?id=<URL-encoded-endpoint-id>&expand=interfaces.attributes&forceDeviceAttributeQuery=true to request permitted device-backed state. Inspect attributes and partial errors. Check sampledAt against the command time and the capability version. sampledAt is the source-reported time, not the fetch time; an absent timestamp means freshness is unknown. Use [enumerateEndpoints and its linked components](/docs/for-ai/operations/enumerateEndpoints.md) for exact response shapes. Report returned device state separately from dispatch acceptance. Stale/unavailable state means unknown, and user confirmation may be necessary for a physical device.

For first setup, test one explicitly selected safe light. Do not turn off all homes as a connectivity check. See [lighting](/docs/for-ai/guides/lighting.md), [first setup](/docs/for-ai/guides/first-setup.md) and [authorization rules](/docs/for-ai/guides/authorization-rules.md).

title: How to react to device events
description: Use this guide when an application or agent needs to react when a device changes state.
content:
# How to react to device events

Subscribe to a device event, such as motion at the front door, so your AI or your application can react when it happens.

## What you need

- A Port OS account and a connected device that reports the event you want. A camera that detects motion is an example.
- An AI client connected with [MCP](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/how-to-use-mcp/), or an application that uses the [REST API](https://portoperatingsystem.com/api/).
- The `subscription:read` and `subscription:write` permissions. Approve them when your AI client asks to connect. A connection approved before these permissions existed must be approved again.

## Availability

Event subscriptions through MCP work only in ChatGPT today, and only for accounts on the waitlist. Other AI clients cannot create subscriptions yet. To join the waitlist, [request access](mailto:support@portoperatingsystem.com?subject=Event%20subscriptions%20waitlist). The REST API manages subscriptions regardless of your AI client.

## Subscribe through your AI

1. Ask your AI to watch for something. For example: "Tell me when someone comes to the front door."
2. Your AI finds the events your devices can report and creates a subscription. Port OS gives the subscription a name you can recognize.
3. When the event happens, Port OS tells your AI, and your AI reacts. For example, it checks the camera and notifies you.

Port OS verifies the connection with your AI before it turns a subscription on. A subscription does not expire unless you set an expiry.

## Manage subscriptions through your AI

These MCP tools list and change the subscriptions you already have:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `subscription_list` | Lists your subscriptions with their IDs, names, source device, event and status. Pass `cursor` to read the next page. |
| `subscription_inspect` | Shows one subscription by its ID, including its filter and status. |
| `subscription_label_edit` | Renames one subscription. To change what is watched, create a new subscription and cancel the old one. |
| `subscription_cancel` | Stops one subscription by its ID. To watch again, create a new subscription. |

Always use the exact ID from `subscription_list`. A name or a device ID does not identify a subscription.

For example, to stop watching the front door, ask your AI: "Stop telling me about the front door." Your AI lists your subscriptions, picks the matching one, and cancels it by ID.

## Manage subscriptions with the REST API

Use these operations to manage subscriptions from your own application. Each one is documented in full in the [REST reference](https://portoperatingsystem.com/api/).

| Operation | Request | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enumerateSubscriptions` | `GET /subscriptions` | Lists subscriptions, or reads one when you pass `id`. |
| `upsertSubscription` | `POST /subscriptions` | Creates or updates a subscription. A subscription has a `query` that selects events and a `target` that receives them. |
| `patchSubscription` | `PATCH /{namespace}/{principalType}/{principalId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` | Renames a subscription. |
| `deleteSubscription` | `DELETE /{namespace}/{principalType}/{principalId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` | Stops a subscription. |

A subscription can include a `context` filter. Each key is a path into the message, such as `header.namespace` or `header.name`, and each value is what the message must contain. A subscription fires only when every entry matches. Leave `context` out to receive every event.

Saving a subscription is eventually consistent. A saved subscription means Port OS registered it. It does not prove that your AI or application received an event. Read it back with `GET /subscriptions` and check that its `status` is `ACTIVE`.

## Subscription status

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ACTIVE` | The subscription is watching. |
| `PAUSED` | The subscription is on hold. |
| `SUSPENDED` | Delivery is suspended. The reason code explains why. |
| `EXPIRED` | The subscription reached its expiry time. |
| `STOPPED` | You or the system cancelled the subscription. |

## Troubleshooting

- **Your AI cannot create a subscription.** Check that your AI client supports event subscriptions and that your account is on the waitlist.
- **A request returns 403 `insufficient_scope`.** The error names the missing permission. Reconnect your AI client and approve `subscription:read` and `subscription:write`.
- **A subscription stopped after you reconnected your AI.** Port OS stops subscriptions when you revoke the connection that created them. Create the subscription again.
- **You get no events.** Check that the subscription is `ACTIVE`, that the device is online, and that you can see the source device. See [authorization rules](/docs/for-ai/guides/authorization-rules.md).

content:
# Reading the Port OS documentation

Port OS connects device providers to endpoints you can query and control. Start at [the agent index](/docs/for-ai/index.md). You do not need to sign in to read public documentation.

1. Read [authentication and DCR](/docs/for-ai/guides/authentication-and-dcr.md) to connect.
2. Follow [quickstart](/docs/for-ai/guides/quickstart.md) to verify authorized access.
3. Choose a task guide, then follow its operation and capability links.

Files under /docs/for-ai/ are Markdown. Files under /docs/references/ ending in .yaml are raw contracts. /docs/user-guides/ contains human-readable HTML versions of these guides. A document link is information, not authorization to act. User sign-in and consent occur only on the Port OS account page.

Use [the OpenAPI contract](/docs/references/openapi.yaml) for exact paths, fields and results and [the capability index](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces.md) for message payloads. Do not read the entire reference when one operation or capability page answers your question.

title: Sign in and connect your accounts
description: Use this guide when a customer wants to sign in, connect device accounts and let their AI use them.
content:
# Sign in and connect your accounts

Sign in to Port OS, connect your device accounts, and let your AI use them. You choose what each connection can do, and you can remove it later.

## Sign in to Port OS

1. Open [Port OS](https://portoperatingsystem.com/sign-in/) and choose Sign in with Google.
2. Approve the Google sign-in. Port OS opens your dashboard.

You do not need a separate Port OS password. If someone else needs temporary access, for example a reviewer, create a [website access key](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/user-guides/how-to-set-up-test-access-keys-for-port-os/) for them instead of sharing your account.

## Connect your device accounts

Port OS reaches your devices through the accounts you already have with their makers, such as your Spotify or smart home account.

1. Open the [plugin catalog](https://portoperatingsystem.com/plugins/) and choose your provider.
2. Choose Connect. Sign in on the provider's own page. Port OS never sees your provider password.
3. Approve the access the provider asks for.
4. Open [Your devices](https://portoperatingsystem.com/dashboard/) and check that your devices appear.

If a device is missing, reconnect the provider. Not every device supports every action, so check what your device can do before you rely on it.

## Let your AI use Port OS

1. Add Port OS to your AI client. See [How to use MCP](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/how-to-use-mcp/) or choose your client in the [connection guides](https://portoperatingsystem.com/connect-ai/).
2. Your AI client sends you to Port OS to sign in. Review the access it asks for.
3. Choose Allow to approve it, or Deny to cancel.

You can allow some access and refuse the rest. For example, let your AI list your devices without letting it control them. Port OS shows the app's name, but an app can choose any name. Approve only apps you started yourself.

## Remove a connection

- To remove a provider, open the [plugin catalog](https://portoperatingsystem.com/plugins/), choose the provider, and disconnect it.
- To stop an AI client or app, open [Tokens](https://portoperatingsystem.com/tokens/) and revoke its connection. Port OS then rejects its next request.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Port OS asks you to sign in again | Your sign-in expired. Sign in again. |
| Your AI says access is denied | Reconnect it and allow the access it asked for. |
| A provider shows as disconnected | Reconnect it. Providers sometimes end a connection after a password change. |
| You do not recognize an app asking for access | Choose Deny. |

## For developers

Building your own app or client? See the OAuth guides for developers:

- [Set up an OAuth client](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/user-guides/how-to-set-up-an-oauth-client-for-port-os/)
- [Register a client with DCR or CIMD](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/user-guides/how-to-register-an-oauth-client/)
- [Scopes and authorization rules](https://portoperatingsystem.com/docs/user-guides/how-to-set-up-access-rules-for-port-os/)

title: Connect SmartThings
description: Use this guide when the customer wants to link SmartThings to read and control SmartThings devices, or to replace an old personal access token connection.
content:
# Connect SmartThings

Link SmartThings to Port OS to read and control your SmartThings devices. You can link it two ways:

- **Your own SmartThings app** (`customer-oauth`): you register an OAuth-In app with the SmartThings CLI and give Port OS its client ID and secret. Available to any account.
- **Port OS's registration** (`portos-oauth`): Port OS uses its own SmartThings app. This is available only to accounts that Port OS has granted access.

The website flow saves first, then authorizes: you save the client ID and secret as a draft connection, then choose Authorize. Nothing is connected until SmartThings returns and Port OS completes the link.

## Use your own SmartThings app [#customer-oauth]

1. Install the [SmartThings CLI](https://developer.smartthings.com/docs/sdks/cli) and sign in.
2. In Port OS, open the SmartThings connect screen and choose the option to use your own SmartThings app. Copy the Redirect URI it shows.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-portos-connect-redirect -->
3. Run `smartthings apps:create` and choose "OAuth-In App" when asked for the app type.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-cli-apps-create -->
4. Enter the Redirect URI from step 2, and select the scopes listed below.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-cli-scopes -->
5. Copy the OAuth client ID and client secret the CLI prints. The secret is shown once.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-cli-credentials -->
6. In Port OS, paste the client ID and client secret and choose Save. This creates a draft; the secret is stored on the backend and never shown again.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-portos-save-credentials -->
7. Choose Authorize. SmartThings asks you to choose a location and approve access; approve it. Port OS then shows SmartThings as connected.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-consent -->

### Redirect URI

The redirect URI registered with the app must match the value the Port OS connect screen shows, character for character, including the scheme, host, path and any trailing slash. SmartThings sends you back to the Port OS auth host, which relays the result to the website.

### Required scopes

Select these scopes when you register the app:

- `r:devices:*`
- `w:devices:*`
- `x:devices:*`
- `r:locations:*`

## Use Port OS's registration [#portos-oauth]

If your account has been granted Port OS's SmartThings registration, the connect screen offers a Port OS registration option. You do not register an app or enter a client ID, secret or Redirect URI.

1. Open the SmartThings connect screen and choose the Port OS registration option.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-portos-oauth-choice -->
2. Choose Authorize and approve the requested access on SmartThings.
   <!-- screenshot: smartthings-portos-oauth-consent -->

If the option is missing, your account has not been granted access. Use your own SmartThings app instead.

## Personal access tokens

Personal access tokens (PATs) are no longer supported for SmartThings. An old SmartThings link that uses a personal access token stops working and must be deleted and connected again. Delete that link and connect SmartThings again with OAuth, either Port OS's app or your own. Revoke the old token in your SmartThings account when you no longer need it.

## Troubleshooting

- **Redirect mismatch.** The app's redirect URI differs from the one Port OS shows. Copy it again from the connect screen and update the app with the SmartThings CLI (`smartthings apps:oauth:update`).
- **Invalid client (`invalid_client`).** The client ID or secret is wrong, or the secret was regenerated. Re-enter both and save again before authorizing.
- **`AUTH_LINK_NOT_READY`.** The connection is still a draft that is missing required values, usually the client secret. Save both client ID and secret, then authorize.
- **Missing devices or permission errors.** The app was registered without all four scopes. Update the app's scopes, then delete the connection and connect again.
- **Connection stops working.** The connection used a personal access token. See Personal access tokens.
- **Stale callback.** An authorization that was started earlier, or opened twice, can return after it expired or was replaced. Close the tab and choose Authorize again.

title: Connect Spotify
description: Use this guide when the customer wants to link Spotify to search music, manage playlists or control Spotify Connect devices.
content:
# Connect Spotify

Link Spotify to Port OS to search music, manage playlists and control Spotify Connect devices. You can link it two ways:

- **Your own Spotify app** (`customer-oauth`): you create an app in the Spotify developer dashboard and give Port OS its client ID and secret. Available to any account, subject to Spotify's development-mode limits (see Quota and development mode).
- **Port OS's registration** (`portos-oauth`): Port OS uses its own Spotify app. This is available only to accounts that Port OS has granted access.

The website flow saves first, then authorizes: you save the client ID and secret as a draft connection, then choose Authorize. Nothing is connected until Spotify returns and Port OS completes the link.

## Use your own Spotify app [#customer-oauth]

1. Sign in to the [Spotify developer dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard) and choose Create app.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-dashboard-create-app -->
2. Give the app a name and description. For APIs used, select Web API.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-dashboard-app-details -->
3. In Port OS, open the Spotify connect screen and choose Use my own Spotify app. Copy the Redirect URI it shows.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-portos-connect-redirect -->
4. Paste that value into the app's Redirect URIs in the dashboard and save.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-dashboard-redirect-uri -->
5. Open the app's settings in the dashboard and copy the client ID and the client secret.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-dashboard-credentials -->
6. In Port OS, paste the client ID and client secret and choose Save. This creates a draft; the secret is stored on the backend and never shown again.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-portos-save-credentials -->
7. Choose Authorize. Spotify asks you to approve the requested access; approve it. Port OS then shows Spotify as connected.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-consent -->

### Redirect URI

The Redirect URI in the Spotify dashboard must match the value the Port OS connect screen shows, character for character, including the scheme, host, path and any trailing slash. Spotify sends you back to the Port OS auth host, which relays the result to the website. Use the value the screen shows, not one copied from elsewhere.

### Required scopes

Port OS requests these scopes. You do not configure scopes in the dashboard; approve them on the Spotify consent screen.

- `user-read-playback-state`
- `app-remote-control`
- `user-modify-playback-state`
- `playlist-read-private`
- `playlist-read-collaborative`
- `playlist-modify-private`
- `playlist-modify-public`
- `user-library-modify`

### Quota and development mode

New Spotify apps start in development mode. Under Spotify's July 2026 update, only users on the app's allowlist can sign in until Spotify grants the app extended quota. Add every Spotify account you want to connect to the allowlist in the dashboard (User Management). Quota limits are counted by Spotify, not Port OS; see Spotify's [quota modes](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/concepts/quota-modes) and the [July 2026 Web API quota update](https://developer.spotify.com/blog/2026-07-23-web-api-quota-updates) for current limits.

## Use Port OS's registration [#portos-oauth]

If your account has been granted Port OS's Spotify registration, the connect screen offers Use Port OS's Spotify app. You do not create a dashboard app or enter a client ID, secret or Redirect URI.

1. Open the Spotify connect screen and choose Use Port OS's Spotify app.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-portos-oauth-choice -->
2. Choose Authorize and approve the requested access on Spotify.
   <!-- screenshot: spotify-portos-oauth-consent -->

If the option is missing, your account has not been granted access. Use your own Spotify app instead.

## Troubleshooting

- **Redirect mismatch (Spotify shows "INVALID_CLIENT: Invalid redirect URI").** The dashboard Redirect URI differs from the one Port OS shows. Copy it again from the connect screen and save the dashboard app.
- **Invalid client (`invalid_client`).** The client ID or secret is wrong, or the secret was regenerated. Re-enter both from the dashboard and save again before authorizing.
- **`AUTH_LINK_NOT_READY`.** The connection is still a draft that is missing required values, usually the client secret. Save both client ID and secret, then authorize.
- **Spotify refuses sign-in for your account.** The app is in development mode and your Spotify account is not on its allowlist. See Quota and development mode.
- **Stale callback.** An authorization that was started earlier, or opened twice, can return to Port OS after it expired or was replaced. Close the tab and choose Authorize again to start a fresh attempt; the previous one is not reused.

title: Control thermostat settings
description: Use this guide when the customer wants to read or set a thermostat target, mode or temperature.
content:
# Control thermostat settings

Discover the intended thermostat and its declared capabilities from [the directory](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces.md). Retrieve the exact setpoint/mode schema before sending. Preserve declared units, supported mode names and temperature bounds; never assume Celsius/Fahrenheit.

Use [authorized REST dispatch](/docs/for-ai/guides/quickstart.md). Read fresh mode/setpoint/temperature observations after the command. A committed target setting does not prove the room has reached that temperature. Report delayed or unavailable observations honestly and do not repeat relative adjustments after an unknown response.

title: Recover from connection and device failures
description: Use this guide when a connection, a device command or a provider link fails and the customer needs the cause and a fix.
content:
# Recover from connection and device failures

First identify the failure boundary: documentation retrieval, registration, user authorization, token validation, scope, resource policy, payload, provider link or device observation.

| Symptom | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| Guide returns a login page/app shell | Use the raw Markdown link from the guide index; report the broken link to support |
| DCR invalid metadata | Correct callback, auth method, supported grants/scopes; do not invent a secret |
| Callback state/issuer mismatch | Stop; discard the response and restart authorization securely |
| Token expired | Refresh with the same client/resource or ask for renewed user consent |
| Scope/policy denied | Read [authorization rules](/docs/for-ai/guides/authorization-rules.md); user/owner must approve access |
| Empty inventory | Valid connection can have no devices; check linking/sharing without guessing IDs |
| Invalid payload | Retrieve the exact capability version/schema and correct the request |
| Provider credential expired | Ask the user to relink the provider account |
| Stale/unavailable state | Report timestamp and uncertainty; do not claim physical completion |
| Lost command response | Recover existing receipt/readback; retry only under documented replay guarantees |
| Committed cleanup pending | Read the committed state/result before any retry |

See [API behavior](/docs/for-ai/guides/using-the-api.md). Never include tokens, provider secrets or another user's private resources in diagnostics.

title: Using the REST API
description: Use this guide to call the Port OS REST API: base URL, authentication, requests and errors.
content:
# Using the REST API

Discover authorization metadata, then use [OAuth setup](/docs/for-ai/guides/authentication-and-dcr.md).
Start with the [compact API catalog](/docs/for-ai/api-catalog.md). It
contains auth context, public operation links, parameter names and top-level JSON
keys. Obtain exact REST paths from its links or the [small operation index](/docs/for-ai/operations/index.md).
Follow one operation's linked schemas for required/conditional fields and
nested payloads. It does not inline all schemas or examples.

For SDK generation or a comprehensive contract download, request the
[full OpenAPI document](/docs/references/openapi.yaml).

The website's `/api/` route serves this compact Markdown when the request puts
`text/markdown` first in `Accept` (for example,
`text/markdown, text/plain;q=0.9, text/html;q=0.8`). Browser HTML requests keep the
interactive reference. Add `?full=1` to explicitly retrieve the complete HTML
catalog; keep HTML in your accepted formats for that request. Both variants
include `Vary: Accept` for caches. The direct compact Markdown URL works on both
the website and API host and does not depend on negotiation.

Enumerate endpoints with endpoint:read. Follow returned pagination links/tokens exactly and stop only when continuation is absent. Inspect declared capabilities and versions; retrieve one message/attribute schema as needed. Send messages through POST /messages (the existing /messages/send alias also works). Never invent target IDs or message fields.

POST /endpoint-query with `{}` defaults to the caller's enabled endpoints, as do type and capability filters. An explicit owner, endpoint ID, or authorized group selector can include readable shared endpoints. Its query accepts exact match and nested and/or/not predicates; read the request schema's supported fields rather than inventing comparisons or text search. A groupId predicate additionally needs group:read and access to that group. Keep the query, page size, expansions, forceDeviceQuery setting and grant unchanged while following paginationContext.nextToken. Empty pages can have a continuation. Cursors expire after fifteen minutes; restart without nextToken on a 400 cursor error.

Use `GET /relationships` to inspect typed edges between endpoints, routes, groups and group routes. It defaults to the caller's relationships, supports resource and type filters, and uses bounded pagination. Both ends of an edge must be readable for it to appear. Endpoint membership in a group is represented by `MEMBER_OF`; change membership through the declared group operation or provider discovery, not by writing arbitrary relationship rows.

REST dispatch and subsequent physical observation are separate facts. A 202 describes unfinished work. A timeout can mean the operation already acted; inspect existing results/state before repeating. IR/Bluetooth fire-and-forget and long-delay devices may never provide immediate confirmation. Use bounded polling and report unresolved state. An endpoint edit marked committed with cleanup pending must not be repeated as though it failed.

Use documented idempotency/correlation and version preconditions only where the operation guarantees them. Setting a value and incrementing it have different replay risks. On an ambiguous lost relative-command response, report unknown or read back rather than blindly send again.

Read [authorization rules](/docs/for-ai/guides/authorization-rules.md), [lighting](/docs/for-ai/guides/lighting.md) or the relevant task guide.

title: Control vacuums and cleaning rooms
description: Use this guide when the customer wants a robot vacuum to start, stop, return to the dock or clean particular rooms.
content:
# Control vacuums and cleaning rooms

Find the robot endpoint and inspect its robotic-vacuum-cleaner and related capability declarations in [the directory](/docs/for-ai/capability-interfaces.md). Supported operations vary by provider; do not infer room cleaning, scheduling or modes from a device name.

Use supported start/stop/mode schemas and full IDs. Spatial cleaning targets the robot endpoint with its supported room/zone payload; an endpoint group is not automatically a robot room. Check constraints and [dispatch semantics](/docs/for-ai/guides/using-the-api.md). Query fresh status afterward; accepted work is not completed cleaning. Ask for clarification when room mappings are ambiguous.

## Select rooms on the website

- [ ] Select a room on the robot's map to highlight it. Select it again to deselect it, or use Clear to remove all selections. Selecting a room does not send a command.
- [ ] Select several rooms only when the robotic-vacuum-cleaner configuration advertises `supportsMultiRoomCleaning: true`; otherwise selection is limited to one room. Only groups the robot can clean are selectable.
- [ ] Use Clean selected to send one `clean-room` command to the robot with the `groupIds` of the selected rooms. Check fresh state afterward; request acceptance does not establish completed cleaning.

## Start and end remote movement

- [ ] Prefer `unary-move` for a bounded movement with working live camera feedback. Roborock owns start, native readiness, five-second startup settling, fresh readiness revalidation, ordered moves and session end.
- [ ] Keep movement duration in milliseconds and preserve its requested bound. Startup settling adds time before motion, not extra motion.
- [ ] Explicit `start-session` acknowledgement does not establish readiness. Advanced callers must verify healthy native manual mode, settle for five seconds and recheck before a `move`; a generic RUNNING state alone is insufficient. Use `unary-move` when those native checks are unavailable.
- [ ] Explicit `move` uses increasing `seqNum` values, beginning at 1 for a new session. `stop-session` stops movement; `end-session` exits manual mode. End an explicitly started session after success or failure, including cancellation, and before requesting docking.
- [ ] Send one-way remote controls with dispatch-acceptance intent (`FIRE_FORGET` in REST; omit MCP `waitForResult`). This still reports dispatch errors. Do not wait for a nonexistent reply or automatically retry an uncertain physical move.

name: connected-home
title: Connected home requests
content:
---
name: connected-home
description: Use for connected-device requests such as turning off lights or a room switch, lowering the thermostat temperature, checking the temperature right now, vacuuming a room, playing or pausing music on Echo/Alexa, lowering speaker volume, looking at a kitchen camera, finding or pinging a phone, or checking whether a phone/watch is dead or needs charging. For a bare temperature question with no indoor/outdoor context, clarify which before assuming weather. Explicit weather forecasts or city temperatures do not require this workflow.
---

# Connected home requests

Resolve the customer's intended home task and use the existing Port OS connection.
Do this workflow in the current chat without delegation.

For "what's the temperature right now?" with no context distinguishing indoor
temperature from weather, ask whether the customer means indoors or outside.
Do not require a city/ZIP before resolving that distinction. For explicit indoor
requests, discover a thermostat/temperature sensor and read ambient temperature;
a setpoint is not a room measurement. Respect explicit outdoor/weather intent.

Read the task guide index at `references/index.md` and the relevant bundled reference:
temperature, lighting, cameras, rooms, media, battery, find-phone, files or reminders.
These are the same Markdown guides published on the website and exposed as MCP
resources at portos://guides/{topic}. When references are unavailable, read
portos://guides/index with resources/read. The guides explain capability selection,
documented payload fields, verification and operation limits; do not invent commands from product names.

Use host-listed account labels to choose the likely authorized home-device
connection. If discovery misses a device, check relevant authorized connections
before denying availability. Keep the returning account with every endpoint,
route and item ID. Ask which account/target before writing when several match.
Do not create connections or expand permissions just to resolve discovery.

For phone/watch battery, charging or Find My requests, inspect every matching
candidate's routes before choosing an exact endpoint. Prefer the concrete device
with an authorized Apple iCloud route for Apple Find My, rather than the first
matching name, an Alexa proxy, a generic plugin or an old unrouted record. If a
same-name record has unavailable data, continue to the relevant route-backed
candidate before claiming iCloud has no reading. Preserve old records; discovery
does not authorize deleting or merging them.

Use declared endpoint_query expansions with forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true for
current state. Missing, stale or unavailable readings mean current state is
unknown. Inspect camera snapshot pixels before describing a scene. Accepted
control alone does not confirm a physical outcome; verify fresh observations and
do not automatically repeat state changes.

For cameras that declare RTC streaming but no on-demand snapshot, prefer the
embedded endpoint_show panel's supported live-view control. Showing a panel does
not establish that video started or that you inspected it. If the host cannot
operate or inspect the embedded viewer, report that limitation. A separate
website may use a different signed-in account; its missing-device result does
not establish that the MCP account lacks the camera.

Explain results and needed clarification in plain customer language. Do not
explain that an internal skill requires a question.

name: setup
title: Set up Port OS
content:
---
name: setup
description: Help connect the Port OS cloud plugin, sign in, authorize access and verify the customer's connected devices.
---

# Set up Port OS

Port OS runs in the cloud. Use the plugin's configured remote MCP connection;
do not install or start a local MCP server, ask for local filesystem access, or
download a runtime.

If the host requests authentication, let the customer complete Port OS sign-in
and consent in their browser. Use Google sign-in. Where the sign-in page offers
access keys, they can also paste a Website sign-in key created on their Tokens
page. Never request the key in chat,
put it in a URL or package, approve consent yourself, or ask for provider MFA.

Provider connections are managed on Port OS. A provider may require its own
sign-in and verification; plugin installation does not establish those links.

After the host confirms connection, use endpoint_query to list authorized
devices. An empty inventory means the account has no visible devices; do not
claim authentication failed. If the customer needs to link a provider, point
them to their Port OS account and its connection UI.

Do not issue a physical command as an installation test. If the customer asks
to test control, discover one explicitly selected device and its declared
capabilities, perform the requested action once, and read fresh observations.
Dispatch acceptance is not proof of physical completion.

If authorization expires or is revoked, use the host's normal reconnect flow.
Revoking a website key stops that key's sign-in/API use. An OAuth connection
already approved with it is a separate grant that the customer revokes
separately. Do not invent refresh tokens for website keys.

title: Check phone, Watch and tracker batteries
content:
# Check phone, Watch and tracker batteries

For "is my phone dead?", "check my Apple Watch", or "should I charge it?":

1. Discover phone/iPhone/Watch names and inspect provider routes plus battery/connectivity interfaces. If a broad query finds Tile/Alexa tracker records as well as Apple iCloud, select the intended Apple device. Prefer its current route-backed record rather than obsolete reconnect duplicates. An endpoint type TRACKER can represent a phone or Watch; do not filter only for PHONE.
2. Query its copied exact endpointId with expand:["battery","connectivity"] and forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true, using only declared capabilities. No control command or phone sound is needed for this question.
3. Interpret each observation separately. Battery level 0 with status available is reported zero; available reachability UNREACHABLE means offline. Offline alone does not prove the battery is depleted. An unavailable/stale/missing battery is unknown, not 0%. Missing sampledAt means no provider measurement time is supplied.
4. Recommend charging for reported zero/low battery; for offline with unknown battery, say it could need charging or reconnection rather than claiming it is dead. Relay the actual percentage and reachability. Do not claim freshness beyond the available forced-read result when Apple exposes no measurement timestamp.
5. For "ping my phone" or "find my phone", read portos://guides/find-phone. That guide distinguishes a requested sound from a location lookup. A battery question does not request either; do not send a locator command or query precise location merely to read battery.

AUTHORIZATION_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRED asks the user to sign in again when automatic recovery cannot renew the account; it does not mean the device battery is dead. Charging notifications require a separately requested monitor/schedule; a one-time battery question does not create one.

title: Look at a kitchen camera or check a room
content:
# Look at a kitchen camera or check a room

"What's going on in my kitchen" can mean room-device state or camera activity. Discover kitchen endpoints and group membership with endpoint_query/group_query, checking relevant authorized accounts when the first lacks a match. Search snapshot capability and camera provider/channel aliases when a literal Kitchen name is absent. A camera's room association establishes the target; unrelated Ring/Swann channels are not proof that a kitchen camera was found. Ask the user which camera/channel if identity remains ambiguous.

For a camera that declares snapshot/get-snapshot, call control with its copied full id and get-snapshot message ID, payload {}, and waitForResult=true. Inspect the returned image pixels before describing what is visible, and report timeOfSample and uncertainty. A snapshot is not a live feed or proof that an event is occurring now. If permission, connection, provider or image retrieval fails, report the limitation without inventing a scene. Do not infer occupancy from lights or a device name.

For device-state questions, force a read of only declared attributes such as connectivity, power or media-player. Stale, missing or unavailable data cannot establish current activity. If only historical values are returned, label them historical and say current state is unknown. Never send household controls merely to observe a room.

For "record 30 seconds" or a snapshot from an RTC-only camera, a live-video command alone does not save an artifact. The Port OS website's live viewer provides Take snapshot and Record 30 seconds, followed by Download snapshot or Download video. Start the stream and wait for actual video frames before capturing. The clip uses remote video only, stays in browser memory until downloaded, and has a 32 MiB limit. Interrupted, empty or oversized recordings are discarded. Stop the stream when finished. These browser controls are distinct from the control snapshot command; do not send undeclared recording commands or claim the MCP API saved a clip. A failed capture does not justify substituting an unrelated camera.

Roborock cameras declare authorization-requirements separately from RTC. Query the declared requirement's configuration status if camera authorization is missing. The customer sets the pattern once in the website's Saved camera pattern settings; the server stores it encrypted and supplies it automatically to permitted snapshots and video. Never request the pattern in chat or put it in an RTC payload. A saved pattern is not proof that the vendor accepted it; report a failed camera request accurately.

For "explore my house", "drive toward the kitchen" or "draw my floor plan", use the robot's declared remote-control unary-move operation, not named-room cleaning, and follow the rooms guide's start/move/end checklist. Establish advancing live video before remote driving and inspect the resulting view after each short bounded movement. Fresh snapshots may supplement that feedback; lack of a snapshot capability does not block working live video. Stop when frames or movement outcomes are unavailable, or when the view cannot establish a clear route. End remote control before using the declared return-to-dock command. Maintain a rough visual sketch with uncertainty; images alone do not establish measured distances. Never claim physical exploration or a completed map from a proposed movement sequence.

title: Find connected devices
content:
# Find connected devices

Use endpoint_query for lights, switches/plugs, cameras, thermostats, TVs/speakers, locks, robot vacuums, phones, iPhone, Apple Watch, Find My trackers, Photos/Drive filesystems and reminders. Device capabilities, not the product type alone, establish what you can do.

1. Start with a focused name/category query, for example {"query":{"name":{"like":"phone"}}}. If a name search misses a known category, broaden to synonyms/manufacturer/capability, then an unfiltered inventory if necessary. Follow paginationContext.nextToken until matching results are covered. An unfiltered inventory is appropriate for organizing the whole account.
   If the host lists multiple authorized accounts, use account labels to choose likely candidates and do read-only discovery across relevant connections before saying a device or library is absent. One account's empty result does not establish another account's inventory. Copy the host-provided account selector; never invent a link/account ID or substitute ownerId to cross account boundaries. Retain the account that returned each endpoint/route ID for later calls; clarify account ambiguity before writing.
2. Inspect routes, providerName, interfaces and declared commands. A repeated name is not proof of identity. Prefer the intended provider's current route-backed record; old reconnect records may have no routes. Tile/Alexa and Apple Find My trackers are not interchangeable battery sources.
3. Copy the full endpoint ID. Query that exact endpointId before constructing the documented control payload. Copy message IDs from messages and routeId from the selected provider. outboundMessages are outputs/events, not commands.
4. For current state, expand only declared capabilities and set forceDeviceAttributeQuery=true. A metadata-only query reads no live state. Only status available establishes a reading; stale/unavailable/missing observations are unknown. UNREACHABLE establishes offline when available. Missing sample timestamps do not supply a measurement time.
5. For ambiguous identities or targets, ask which one. Do not rename, merge or delete endpoint records merely to answer a state question.

For camera images use control with the declared get-snapshot message, payload {} and waitForResult=true and read the cameras guide. For temperature read the temperature guide: use temperature-sensor ambient measurements rather than thermostat setpoints, and clarify indoor versus outdoor when context is ambiguous. Echo/Alexa endpoints may be VOICE_ASSISTANT with media-player and speaker capabilities; inspect commands before denying music control. For lock/PIN or other sensitive controls inspect the documented payload fields and follow user authorization. Use the lighting, battery, files, media or rooms guide for those workflows.

title: Browse Photos and Drive; review cleanup
content:
# Browse Photos and Drive; review cleanup

1. Find the intended route-backed Photos or Drive filesystem with endpoint_query. Personal and shared Photos libraries are separate endpoints. Read the exact endpointId; use only declared filesystem-provider commands through control with waitForResult:true.
   Search filesystem-provider capability and Photos/Drive names across relevant host-listed authorized connections before claiming no library exists. Generic ENDPOINT_PLUGIN catalogs and old unrouted FILESYSTEM records are not concrete provider routes; ignore them for file operations without deleting or merging them. If only unrouted matches exist in one account, check other relevant authorized accounts. Preserve the returning account with every ID and cursor. Clarify multiple matching libraries before a write.
2. For Drive, list-folder with no folderId lists root; descend using returned folder IDs. For Photos, list-albums discovers albums such as Screenshots; list-folder accepts a returned album ID. Follow returned nextCursor using cursor on the same folder/album. Do not assume a small first page represents all files. Photos pages contain at most 100 assets and resume directly at the provider rank; always follow nextCursor, even when fewer than maxResults were returned. Keep cursor, library and album together. Paging observes a live library: edits during enumeration can shift ranks, so collect candidates before making changes, and refresh their identities before deletion. Old cursors must restart after a pagination version change.
3. Copy the returned itemId into download-file's fileId. Download returns a URI that must be fetched to inspect actual contents. Photos returns an original HTTPS resource URL. Current iCloud Drive downloads are inline and limited to 10 MiB per file; a complete large-file backup is not supported by this adapter. Do not expose signed download URLs in summaries or logs.
4. For screenshot cleanup, prefer the discovered Screenshots album over filename guesses. To classify other images, inspect downloaded contents; name/extension alone does not establish that a photo is disposable. Present candidates/reasons and follow the user's authorized selection/scope.
5. Use delete-file only for items the user authorized deleting. The iCloud adapter trashes Drive nodes and soft-deletes Photos. A cleanup recommendation is not an instruction to delete. Send each deletion once, wait for its correlated response and verify absence by re-listing the same selection; for Photos also account for album membership and library identity. Timeouts leave an unknown outcome, so inspect before considering another action.

For upload, select a concrete Drive route that declares upload-file, use its documented payload fields, including the attached file's actual bytes encoded as base64, destination folderId, name and MIME type. Ask for a missing file or ambiguous destination. The iCloud Drive adapter supports up to 10 MiB decoded, requires the filename extension to match the MIME type, and rejects an existing name instead of overwriting it. Upload once with waitForResult:true; use the returned fileId for readback and re-list the destination. If the result is missing or unconfirmed, inspect the destination before considering another upload. Drive routes may declare rename-file and move-file for files. Copy the current fileId, supply the full new name for rename-file or a discovered destination folderId for move-file, send once with waitForResult:true, and use the returned fileId afterward. Rename and move reject destination name collisions and verify the exact file identity/name in the destination; an unconfirmed result requires re-listing source and destination before another write. Folder rename/move, Photos upload/rename/move, and content replacement remain unsupported by this adapter. A capability's upload-file-response output alone does not establish an upload command; discovery is authoritative.

Collect Photos by unique itemId across pages. The adapter excludes Apple's repeated boundary asset while preserving provider-rank advancement; a filtered page can be empty and still have nextCursor. Concurrent library changes can introduce other overlaps, so report the unique count and do not process the same asset twice.

Reminders uses its own provider capability; only use create/update/delete when declared, since legacy iCloud accounts may expose list-reminders only.

For multiple attached files, preserve each attachment's actual bytes, filename and MIME type; do not reconstruct a binary file from extracted text or a preview. Report one result per file. An existing-name rejection must leave that file untouched and must not prevent truthful reporting of another file's result. Do not rename, overwrite or retry an uncertain write automatically. Verify downloads against the original bytes when available; matching a filename or byte count alone does not establish an exact transfer. The MCP inline-result limit can be lower than the adapter's 10 MiB file limit; inspect the actual transfer result and explain bounded coverage.

title: Ping or find a phone
content:
# Ping or find a phone

For "ping my phone", "ring my phone" or "find my phone", use Port OS's connected Find My device, not a network ping or a guessed messaging tool.

1. Find phone/iPhone names with endpoint_query. Inspect providerName, routes and location-tracker/location capabilities. Prefer the requested provider's current route-backed record over obsolete duplicates. TRACKER may represent a phone. If multiple distinct phones remain, ask which one.
2. "Ping/ring my phone" requests an audible locator. Query the exact endpointId, copy the declared location-tracker command, then send control once on that endpoint/route. iCloud declares start-locator; never invent play-sound or another provider-specific message. An accepted result means the locator was requested, not that the sound was heard. Report that distinction; do not retry automatically.
3. "Find my phone" usually requests help locating it. If a location capability is declared, read the copied exact endpoint with expand:["location","connectivity"] and forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true. Relay an available location and its supplied timestamp; stale data is last-known, not current. Do not claim missing coordinates mean the phone is lost/offline. If a sound would help and location is unavailable, offer to ring it or ask whether the user wants location or sound; do not silently replace an unsuccessful location read with a physical action.
4. A specifically requested ping can be sent without reading precise location. A battery question needs the battery guide and no locator command. If connectivity is available and UNREACHABLE, report the phone offline; command rejection must not be reported as a successful ring. Do not infer a depleted battery from offline alone.

Respect the user's requested target and scope. Avoid copying precise location, account IDs or signed resources into diagnostics. Account authorization errors require connection recovery/sign-in, not guessing new device IDs.

title: Port OS task guide index
content:
# Port OS task guide index

Read the guide that matches the user's task before an unfamiliar workflow. Use MCP resources/read with the URI below, or the matching bundled reference in the Port OS connected-home skill if your client exposes only tools. Guides do not grant permissions or prove a device/action exists; discover the current account's capabilities.

| User request | Resource | Skill reference topic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect the cloud plugin or sign in with a website key | portos://guides/setup | setup |
| Shared connected-home skill and safety/readback workflow | portos://guides/connected-home | connected-home |
| Find/list devices; identify a camera, thermostat, lock, phone or tracker | portos://guides/discovery | discovery |
| Turn off the lights; dim a lamp; check light state | portos://guides/lighting | lighting |
| Lower the temperature; what's the temperature right now? Indoor ambient versus thermostat target | portos://guides/temperature | temperature |
| What's going on in my kitchen? Look at my kitchen camera | portos://guides/cameras | cameras |
| Is my phone dead? Check my Watch battery; should I charge it? | portos://guides/battery | battery |
| Ping my phone; ring my phone; find my phone; locate my lost iPhone | portos://guides/find-phone | find-phone |
| Find screenshots; download Photos; upload, rename or move Drive files; suggest cleanup | portos://guides/files | files |
| Show my Shopping list; what's due today or overdue; add/complete an iCloud reminder | portos://guides/reminders | reminders |
| Play on Echo Dot Max/Alexa; pause the song; lower volume; manage my playlist | portos://guides/media | media |
| Find a room/group; vacuum a room; move Roborock, explore the house or return home | portos://guides/rooms | rooms |

Use endpoint_query for discovery and observations, control for declared commands, endpoint_manage/group_manage for metadata changes. Do not send outboundMessages as commands. Use documented payload fields for the declared command; the backend validates requests. Capability reference resources at portos://capability-interfaces/{name}/{version} publish interface declarations and reference documentation. Do not depend on runtime command input schemas.

Read only the relevant guide, rather than all guides or the entire capability reference. If tools or descriptions are cached from an older connection, the host may need to refresh its connection/discovery. Explain a missing tool honestly; never invent its arguments or fabricate a result.

When several authorized connections exist, use their account labels and read-only discovery to find the relevant library/device before claiming it is missing. IDs belong to the account that returned them; keep that association for later reads and control. If several accounts match a requested write, clarify the intended account. Instructions do not authorize new connections or broader permissions.

For follow-ups such as "it", "that file" or "turn it down", retain the resolved account, target and supported property; clarify an ambiguous referent. Apply corrections and exclusions before dispatch. A timeout leaves an unknown outcome: inspect the destination/device before another write. For multiple targets or files, report each result separately, including failures and unknown outcomes; one success does not establish success for the whole request. A read-only request sends no control commands. Do not promise a future action unless a declared scheduling operation creates a verifiable job.

title: Work with lights and lamps
content:
# Work with lights and lamps

For "turn off the lights", "dim the bedroom lamp" or "are the lights on?":

1. Discover matching names/rooms and inspect power/brightness capabilities. A lamp may be typed LIGHT, SWITCH or PLUG, so an exact LIGHT-only filter can miss it. A PLUG controlling an unrelated appliance is not automatically a light. Exclude generic plugin endpoints; simulator devices do not establish the customer's household light state.
2. If a room/group is requested use group_query to resolve membership; do not assume a room name matches every endpoint name. Follow pagination and choose the requested scope. Clarify only if the target/scope remains ambiguous.
3. Query the exact endpointId. Copy the declared power/brightness command ID and use its documented payload fields; do not guess an on/off boolean or brightness range. Use control on the chosen endpoint/authorized group and preserve routeId when selecting a provider.
4. After an accepted command, query the exact endpoint with expand:["power","connectivity"] and forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true when both are declared. Add brightness for a dimming request. Report confirmed observations, not dispatch acceptance, as the outcome.
5. An available UNREACHABLE reading means offline even if an old power value says ON/OFF. Missing or unavailable readings do not mean OFF. Report an unconfirmed outcome if verification fails. Never automatically repeat a state-changing command after acceptance or timeout.

Read-only light state questions need endpoint_query, not control. Editing names/groups belongs in endpoint_manage/group_manage and is a separate user task.

title: Work with music, speakers and TVs
content:
# Work with music, speakers and TVs

Find the intended speaker/TV or media library with endpoint_query. Inspect the exact endpointId; copy declared command and route IDs. Search music and list/get playlists through control with waitForResult:true when the command returns correlated results. Use the returned media identifiers instead of inventing IDs or treating an output event as a command.

Echo Dot Max/Alexa speakers can be typed VOICE_ASSISTANT and declare media-player and speaker commands. Search names and capabilities before saying Alexa control is unavailable. Check relevant authorized account labels (for example home devices versus iCloud) and retain the account that returned each target. For "this song" without a referent, ask title/artist/link without a blanket capability denial. A declared search-and-play command may accept a song query directly; use its exact documented payload fields rather than inventing a media URI or requiring a separate music library when this route supports direct search.

For pause or lower-volume requests, discover active playback/current speaker volume on matching connected devices; ask which target if several or none can be established. An explicit relative-volume amount is needed unless the device declares a suitable step command with a defined/default amount. Read supported units and payload before sending. Keep playback and volume on the intended provider route.

"Manage my playlist" may mean read, play, curate or edit. Discover media-playlist operations on relevant authorized connections, then ask which playlist and desired change. list-playlists/get-playlist support browsing. Spotify library routes can declare create-playlist, add-to-playlist, remove-from-playlist, rename-playlist and unfollow-playlist. Creation makes a private playlist; tracks must be exact returned Spotify track IDs (up to 100 per call). For removal, Spotify requires trackIndex:-1 and trackUri copied from the listing; this removes all occurrences, so make that scope clear and do not use it for a request to remove only one duplicate. Rename changes the selected owned playlist's name and verifies it by reading back. Unfollow removes the selected playlist from this account's library; it does not permanently delete the provider playlist. Re-list to confirm absence. A playlist-mutation-result acknowledges the provider snapshot; verify requested contents by reading them. applied:false means a partial operation, such as successful creation with unconfirmed initial tracks: preserve the returned playlistId and inspect before another write. Existing connections may need reconnecting to grant playlist-modify-private/public and user-library-modify; a 403 must not be reported as a successful edit. Never repeat an uncertain write automatically. Reordering and permanent playlist deletion are not exposed by this adapter. Other providers may differ; inspect concrete route commands.

Playback, pause and volume use the documented payload fields supported by the chosen provider route. Verify afterward with endpoint_query, declared speaker/media-player/connectivity expansion and forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true. Dispatch acceptance alone does not confirm audible playback. A paused TV is not necessarily powered off. Report stale/unavailable state as unknown and never automatically repeat an accepted state-changing command.

title: Work with reminder lists
content:
# Work with reminder lists

1. For "my iCloud reminders", "my Shopping list" or "what's overdue", discover concrete reminders-provider endpoints on relevant authorized accounts. Preserve the account with each endpoint, list ID, reminder ID and cursor. Ignore generic plugin catalogs and old unrouted records. Read the exact endpoint and copy its route and declared command IDs.
2. Use list-reminders through control with waitForResult:true. Inspect returned list titles and IDs before selecting a named list. If Shopping is absent, report that and ask which existing list to use; do not silently substitute another list or create a new one. Follow pagination for the same filters. An empty result proves only the queried selection is empty, not that every account or completed history is empty.
3. Distinguish iCloud/connected reminder lists from ChatGPT scheduled tasks. An explicitly named service must not be replaced with another service. For a generic reminder request, clarify the intended service when the available choices could change the answer or action.
4. For today, tomorrow or overdue, use the customer's timezone and actual supported due-date fields. Do not infer a due date from a title, note, creation time or completion flag. If the route cannot return due dates, report that limitation; do not claim a complete due/overdue list. If a complete open-item listing is empty, it is safe to say that selection has no open items.
5. Create, update, complete or remove a reminder only when the concrete route declares that command and its payload represents the requested fields. Legacy iCloud routes may be list-only. Outbound create/update responses do not establish writable support. A date written into the title or notes is not a real scheduled due date. Do not create a ChatGPT task as a substitute without the user's instruction.
6. For supported edits, copy IDs and the current revision from a recent listing, preserve omitted fields, dispatch once and independently re-list the same selection. Retain the exact created item for follow-up completion/removal; duplicate titles require disambiguation. A timeout means the outcome is unknown: inspect the list before retrying. Report individual outcomes for batches without repeating successful mutations.

Never claim creation, completion, deletion or notification delivery from dispatch acceptance alone. Unsupported history, dates or writes are capability limitations, not proof that the customer's Apple account has no reminders.

Modern reminder commands also support dueDate as an exact RFC3339 instant, timeZone as an IANA zone, and allDay. Resolve relative dates in the customer's known time zone or clarify it; do not invent a zone. Update preserves omitted date fields. clearDueDate:true explicitly removes a date and cannot be combined with dueDate. Completion uses update-reminder with completed:true and the current revision. Read back the title, completion and due date after mutation; legacy list-only routes cannot perform these operations.

title: Find rooms, groups and robot vacuums
content:
# Find rooms, groups and robot vacuums

Use group_query for room/floor/home membership and parentPath. Use endpoint_query for the requested robot vacuum or other controller and its controllableGroups. Clarify ambiguous rooms/robots; rooms with the same name in different homes are different targets.

Read the documented payload fields for the exact declared endpoint/group command. For robotic vacuum clean-room, send control to the robot endpoint whose controllableGroups contains the requested room, using copied groupIds in the declared payload. Check the robotic-vacuum-cleaner interface configuration: multiple groupIds require supportsMultiRoomCleaning=true. If it is absent or false, select one room. Do not send cleaning to a room endpoint or invent a second action path. Other group controls require that the selected authorized group route advertises the message.

After acceptance verify relevant available fresh observations. Acceptance is not proof that cleaning finished. Do not automatically repeat state-changing commands or report missing state as success. Rename, membership, enablement and merge operations use group_manage/endpoint_manage as a separately authorized metadata task.

## Bounded Roborock movement

- [ ] For "move the Roborock forward", "explore my house", "go to the kitchen" or "go back home", distinguish remote driving, navigation, cleaning and docking. Inspect the declared remote-control messages and read the cameras guide. Establish working, advancing live video before moving.
- [ ] Prefer unary-move with one short instruction. The integration starts one session, waits for native manual/remote mode with error code zero, allows five seconds of firmware startup settling, and requires one fresh healthy manual-mode reading before moving. Lost mode or cancellation prevents movement and triggers bounded cleanup.
- [ ] Use velocity in meters per second (-0.3 to 0.3), omega in radians per second (-0.8 to 0.8), and duration in milliseconds (1–5000). A 300 ms movement remains 300 ms; the startup delay does not lengthen motion. Unary-move assigns sequence numbers and ends its session after the requested movements.
- [ ] Treat acceptance as dispatch evidence, not proof of movement. Inspect the resulting live view before continuing. If the outcome is uncertain, stop and inspect; never automatically repeat a move or enlarge its duration to force a result.

## Explicit start, move and end

- [ ] Keep one robot and provider route throughout the session. start-session acknowledges the native start command; its acknowledgement alone does not establish movement readiness.
- [ ] Advanced callers using explicit start-session/move must verify native manual/remote state and error code zero, allow five seconds of startup settling, then check native readiness again once before moving. A projected RUNNING observation alone cannot distinguish manual mode from cleaning. When native readiness cannot be verified, use unary-move, which owns these checks.
- [ ] Send each bounded move once with an increasing non-negative seqNum; begin a new session at 1. Use the exact documented payload fields instead of guessing units or field names.
- [ ] stop-session stops movement; end-session exits remote-control mode. Explicit callers own cleanup: stop when feedback is lost or an outcome is uncertain, then end the session even after a failed/canceled operation, using a separate bounded cleanup context where applicable. Neither command requests docking.
- [ ] Do not leave an explicit session active or mix direct move commands with a unary-move session. After cleanup, use the declared return-to-dock command if requested and verify fresh docking/charging state.

Room cleaning does not navigate without cleaning. Only use a declared navigation operation for "go to the kitchen"; the current Roborock integration has none. Missing Kitchen membership is not permission to guess another room or coordinates. Explain the limitation and offer supported short remote moves only when visual feedback is available. "Go back home" uses the declared vacuum return-to-dock command after ending remote control; verify fresh docking/charging state instead of equating acceptance with arrival. Unavailable visual feedback, including a blocked camera, prevents visually guided exploration; do not improvise an unseen route. Missing snapshot support alone does not block movement when advancing live video is available.

title: Thermostat and current indoor temperature
content:
# Thermostat and current indoor temperature

For "lower the temperature" or "what's the temperature right now?", determine whether the user means indoor/device temperature or outdoor weather. If context does not decide, ask which; do not silently substitute weather for a connected-home reading.

1. Read-only discovery: endpoint_query for thermostats and temperature-sensor capabilities, with focused room/name queries and pagination. If the host exposes multiple authorized accounts, inspect likely home-device connections before declaring a sensor absent. Keep each account's IDs separate. Ask which room/device if several match.
2. Current temperature means the temperature-sensor ambient reading, not a thermostat setpoint. Read the exact endpoint with declared temperature-sensor/connectivity expansion and forceDeviceAttributeQuery:true. Report available value and units; stale/unavailable readings cannot establish current temperature. Do not infer a temperature from mode, a target or weather.
3. For control, read the exact endpointId and copy the route and declared thermostat command. Clarify desired target or relative amount and units when missing. A relative change uses an available current setpoint, not ambient temperature; if unavailable, ask for an explicit target. Use the documented payload fields; the backend validates the request.
4. Send once and verify fresh thermostat observations. A changed setpoint does not mean the room has already cooled. Accepted dispatch without available verification is unconfirmed; never automatically repeat the change.
